role.altitude: The geoscientist keeps judging ground risks, advising clients, conducting field studies, developing extraction strategies with stakeholders and measuring in the field; requesting borehole data piecemeal, recomputing option tables and copying readings from field books shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A geoscientist who starts every study with all public ground data already on the map.

tasks.short: Gather existing ground data for the site, judge ground risks and form the advice, write the advice, and discuss it to advise construction firms or government agencies on dam or road construction, foundation design, land use or resource management.

steps.what: Geoscientist gathers existing ground data for the site: borehole logs, soundings and geological maps
Geoscientist judges ground risks and forms the advice for construction or land use
Geoscientist advises the construction firm or agency in a meeting

tasks.design: Existing borehole logs, soundings and geological models for the site are retrieved from the national subsurface data service by drawing the site boundary, instead of requesting them file by file. Judging risks and advising stay with the geoscientist. Writing the advice report stays with the geoscientist.
tasks.enabler_now: National subsurface data services queried by area.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a peat layer will make the road settle unevenly.

evidence.claim: National subsurface data services provide borehole logs and soundings by area.

assumptions: Boundary: advising clients; preparing maps and reports (task 3705) and interpreting data (task 3702) are sibling tasks.
s3 is the geoscientist's own advice; it is a first write and keeps its full time. The answer for sibling task 3705 keeps report writing at full time too.
Judging and advising keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of sites with good public data.
research_questions: Does time to first advice fall?

incremental.description: Geoscientist checks retrieved data for gaps.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: sites with little public data; high: well-covered urban sites.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Retrieve existing subsurface data, plan and conduct field investigations, process the data, and draw conclusions to conduct geological or geophysical studies for regional development, site selection or public works.

steps.what: Geoscientist retrieves existing borehole, sounding and geophysical data for the study area
Geoscientist plans and conducts field investigations
Geoscientist processes and models the geological and geophysical data
Geoscientist draws conclusions for site selection or public works

tasks.design: Existing subsurface data for the study area are retrieved from the national data service by area, instead of requests by mail and file. Field work, data processing and conclusions are covered by their own tasks or stay with the geoscientist, so this task changes little.
tasks.enabler_now: National subsurface data services queried by area.
tasks.still_hard: Areas where old data are of unknown quality.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing where to drill to answer the real question.

evidence.claim: National subsurface data services provide borehole logs and soundings by area.

assumptions: Boundary: conducting studies; reviewing reports (task 20390), field studies (task 3703) and analysing data with software (task 15224) are sibling tasks.
s2 is planning and field work and keeps its full time.
s3 is part of analysing geological data with software, which sibling task 15224 covers; its saving is counted there.
unknowns: Share of studies in areas with good public data.

incremental.description: Geoscientist checks retrieved data for gaps.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: remote areas with little data; high: well-covered areas.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review site geology and environmental constraints, compare extraction and reclamation options, develop strategies for more environmentally friendly resource extraction and reclamation with stakeholders, and write the strategy.

steps.what: Geoscientist reviews the site's geology, extraction plan and environmental constraints
Geoscientist compares extraction and reclamation options: volumes, impacts and costs
Geoscientist develops the extraction and reclamation strategy with stakeholders

tasks.design: Protected areas, groundwater protection zones and other constraints from public map services are shown with the site's geological model on one map, instead of collected from separate documents. A scenario sheet linked to volumes from the geological model recalculates impacts and costs per extraction and reclamation option. Developing the strategy with stakeholders stays with the geoscientist. Writing the strategy document stays with the geoscientist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Constraints sat in separate documents and option tables were rebuilt by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Public map services and scenario sheets linked to geological models.
tasks.human_edge: Finding a reclamation plan the community will accept.
tasks.altitude: Less recalculating; developing the strategy stays.

reach.learn: Whether options are compared on the same basis.

evidence.claim: Parameterised models can refresh report tables when inputs change.

assumptions: Boundary: developing strategies; preparing maps and reports (task 3705) is a sibling task.
s4 is the geoscientist's own strategy text; it is a first write and keeps its full time.
Input contract for s2: volumes from the geological model built under task 15224.
Developing with stakeholders keeps its full time.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few options; high: many options and constraints.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Set up and calibrate instruments, measure characteristics of the Earth such as gravity or magnetic fields, record readings and positions, and apply standard corrections.

steps.what: Geoscientist sets up and calibrates gravimeters, magnetometers or seismographs in the field
Geoscientist measures gravity or magnetic fields at each station
Geoscientist records readings, station positions and times
Geoscientist applies drift, tide and terrain corrections to the readings

tasks.design: Setting up, calibrating and measuring stay hands-on. Instruments log each reading with GNSS position and time to a field tablet, instead of the geoscientist writing them in a field book and typing them up. Standard drift, tide and terrain corrections are applied by the processing software, and the geoscientist checks the corrected values.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readings were written in field books and corrected in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Instruments with digital logging and processing software with standard corrections.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing that a station sits on disturbed ground.
tasks.altitude: Less writing and arithmetic; field work stays.

reach.learn: Whether corrected data arrive the same day.

evidence.claim: Field instruments can log readings with GNSS position, and processing software applies standard corrections.

assumptions: Boundary: measuring; interpreting geophysical data (task 3702) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s3: instruments with digital output, about 70% of the instrument park; s3 is priced at that share.
Setting up and measuring keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of instruments with digital logging.

incremental.description: Geoscientist checks logging setup and correction settings per survey.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older instruments; high: digital instruments throughout.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
